rationale_overall: This week's pool produced two genuine nuclear-SMR catalysts worth flagging for future rebalances — Oklo (OKLO) selecting Kiewit as lead contractor for its first commercial Aurora powerhouse in Idaho (concrete commercial milestone), and NuScale (SMR) up 34% W/W on fuel-cell news plus AI-driven power-demand tailwinds — but neither rises to a 'clearly stronger vehicle vs a current holding' bar: none of AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, or NVDA show any thesis-breach, peak-enthusiasm, or obsolescence signal this week (if anything GOOGL and NVDA got incremental positive AI news — Pentagon's $200M AI contract ceiling to Google, and Nvidia's continued China/AI-chip momentum). Per the swap-requires-a-genuine-catalyst-and-a-weakening-holding standard, and with weekly cadence calibrated toward inaction, I filtered out the noise: foreign/OTC-only listings (Black Pearl/B2B Rocket on NZX/ASX, C-COM Satellite Systems, Horizon Robotics HK, Westinghouse as a Brookfield subsidiary with no standalone ticker), private companies (SpaceX, Sierra Space, Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Starlab consortium), pure geopolitical/military events with no investable ticker (Israeli Dror-1 satellite launch, Brahmos missile commentary, Imo State rocket-launcher crackdown, India-Pakistan Kirana Hills satellite imagery, Gaza munition story), routine corporate housekeeping (Uranium Energy Corp's AGM results), vague opinion pieces naming no ticker (Fool.com 'underappreciated AI stock', 'Nvidia-backed AI data center stock'), academic/museum items (Miami University quantum institute, Huntsville Space & Rocket Center donations), and a minor ABB customer order that doesn't rise to a catalyst. Watchlist shape unchanged this period; OKLO and SMR are noted as leading candidates should next week's news confirm a durable SMR buildup and a corresponding softening in one of the AI mega-caps.
